That field is written only at 6333, in the same JudgeLinksPastGuard call that writes _previousPastGuard on the line before, during the same reading, after its reset. So previous always gets the written value.

Same reason as for _previousPastGuard. _streamPastGuard is written only by JudgeLinksPastGuard, which runs only for a non-candidate table that is not named by /XRefStm and whose rows a guard stopped. That reading returns Read and is the last before the check at 3531. So a stale value is never read.

Under the mutant, -2 reaches hybrid only through 'hybrid = _streamPastGuard' (3536), when the stream path alone set pastGuard. Every later read of hybrid in that iteration first tests 'hybrid >= 0' (3543, 3545, 3547, 3595) or goes through hybridReached, which is -1 whenever hybrid < 0 (3557). hybrid is redeclared by the out argument of the next iteration's reading, so -2 and -1 behave the same.

Only the two non-candidate readings pass remember = true, and each position they read was probed and kept just before. At the loop top, ReachedAt calls StartOf(position) for every offset that is in the file and not yet reached, with no probe in between. For an /XRefStm, ReachedAt(hybrid) probes it, and only StartOfNamed's single probe of the /Prev comes between, which pushes it no further than the Before slot. So PaddingAt always answers from _paddingProbes and never reaches its remember branch; the candidates pass false either way.

problems: PFR-0884 was not confirmed by the first harness run. The allocation test b4-05 wrote measured the bytes an opening allocates. In the harness's first filter (3253 tests in one process) it passed with the mutant applied, because the shared ArrayPool<(long, long)> already held arrays of the 4,096-range size from earlier tests and lent one without allocating. So the leaked array cost nothing in that process. Fixed in a new commit, 4327524, which rewrites the test body under the same name. It now watches the pool itself: the file is shaped (40 subsections, every other one empty, then an older stream of 16) so that the array of 32 the newer stream's ranges are kept in is the only array of its size the opening rents. The array the thread gives back just before the opening is lent again after it only if the merge gave it back. This is no longer an allocation measure, so I ran it myself. The rerun reads KILLED.

The fix rests on SharedArrayPool's per-thread slot: a thread is lent first the array of a size it gave back last. The test asserts this as a premise before opening. A gen2 collection under memory pressure can empty those slots, so an opening during which a gen2 collection count changes is done again, up to 5 tries. It holds on net10.0; a change to the runtime's pool would show as the premise failing.
